scorecard.name: Empathy & Acknowledgment Statement
scorecard.coaching: At turn 1 and turn 14, the customer expressed severe frustration over paying £65/month for Fibre 900 while suffering severe peak throttling down to 15 Mbps, but you offered no empathetic validation of her experience.

grader.scenario: Broadband throttling down to 15 Mbps on Fibre 900 package during peak hours
grader.notes: Julian executes master-level network engineering, diagnosing PON optical splitter contention and executing a live virtual circuit migration to an uncrowded XGS-PON port that restores throughput to 885 Mbps. However, he fails Empathy by moving straight to technical checks without acknowledging Hannah's justified frustration.

items.name: Empathy & Acknowledgment Statement
items.evidence: [00:15] Customer: 'I am paying sixty-five pounds a month for your top-tier Fibre 900 package, but every evening between seven PM and ten PM, our download speed collapses down to fifteen megabits!...', Agent moves straight to verification questions without empathy.

items.name: Paraphrasing
items.evidence: [01:10] Agent restated: 'So what I understand is you are subscribed to our Fibre 900 tier, but experience severe speed degradation down to fifteen megabits during peak evening hours...'

items.name: Took ownership of the problem
items.evidence: [03:40] Agent stated: 'I will take direct ownership of this. I have administrative access to the OLT provisioning console, and I can migrate your ONT virtual circuit over to an uncrowded XGS-PON splitter port on card two.'

items.name: Build rapport and observed professionalism
items.evidence: [02:30] Agent maintained a firm, composed, yet thoroughly professional and respectful dialogue throughout, using technical justifications appropriately.
